summary: The operational evidence for this pattern comes from a production agent workspace that keeps its knowledge as living dossiers in the repository, plus an earlier anonymized file-based memory with an index. Both exposed the value of simple storage and the failure modes that remain after storage is solved.

items.text: Agent Studio — The Wiki as Cognitive Interface: the project wiki as a bidirectional interface between repository knowledge and executable work; agents read it for grounding and write back through pipeline steps; archive is a metadata operation that keeps the page readable.

Agent Studio — Wiki Pulse dashboard: the generated landing view that bands every page Fresh, Aging or Stale by commits under the code roots since its last edit, deliberately deterministic and without a model.
Agent Studio — Living document naming: the recorded decision to call the artifact a dossier in UI and documentation while keeping workbench identifiers, descriptors, routes and keys unchanged.
Durable facts were stored one per file, indexed from a small entry point and connected with explicit links. Operators could review changes with the same diff and history tools used for code.
Corrections were written as successors to older entries. Keeping the supersession link preserved provenance while giving recall a clear current answer.
Recall became debuggable when the system displayed the selected memory paths and relevant excerpts. Before that change, operators could observe an answer but not the beliefs that shaped it.

Three recurring incidents remained: stale memory recommended command-line flags that no longer existed, beliefs used during a run were invisible to the operator, and the index drifted away from the files it was meant to expose.
